skill.name: golang-context
skill.description: Guides idiomatic Go context propagation, cancellation, deadlines, request-scoped values, and background work across HTTP handlers, services, and databases.
skill.summary: Review and improve Go context lifecycles across request boundaries.
skill.author: samber

security_audit.summary: All 49 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, Go identifiers, metadata, or illustrative evaluation fixtures. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, system reconnaissance, or unauthorized command execution. One semantic risk remains: the background audit example removes cancellation and deadlines without bounding its goroutine lifetime.

remediation.issue: Detached audit work has no timeout or shutdown cancellation.
remediation.suggestion: Derive a finite timeout from WithoutCancel inside the goroutine and defer cancellation; document concurrency limits and graceful shutdown ownership.

semantic_findings.title: Detached Audit Work Has No Lifetime Bound
semantic_findings.description: The recommended audit goroutine uses context.WithoutCancel without a replacement timeout or shutdown signal. Blocked audit calls can accumulate goroutines and connections across requests.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: WithoutCancel removes the inherited deadline and cancellation signal, and the example supplies no replacement bound. Resource exhaustion depends on the audit implementation and request volume.

content.user_title: Improve Go Context Propagation and Cancellation
content.value_statement: Broken context propagation leaves downstream work running after requests end. This skill guides context lifecycles across Go handlers, services, and databases.
actual_capabilities: Guide context propagation from HTTP handlers through services to database and HTTP client calls.
Explain cancellation ownership, timeout cleanup, nested deadlines, and cancellation checks in loops.
Review context-aware database calls, including transaction creation with BeginTx.
Show typed context keys and separate request metadata from explicit dependencies.
Explain WithoutCancel and AfterFunc for detached work and cancellation-triggered cleanup.
Illustrate request trace propagation through middleware and outbound HTTP headers.
limitations: Provides guidance and illustrative snippets, not a standalone analyzer or executable Go package.
WithoutCancel and AfterFunc examples require Go 1.21 or later.
Several snippets omit application types, imports, and implementation details; generated changes require compilation and tests.
Detached work examples omit lifetime bounds and do not guarantee audit delivery or graceful shutdown.

output: Transaction creation does not receive the caller context.

output_examples.input: Explain why an asynchronous audit event stops when its HTTP handler returns.
output: The goroutine inherits a request context that is canceled when the handler returns.
WithoutCancel preserves request values while removing cancellation and deadlines.
Add a finite timeout and shutdown ownership; detaching cancellation alone does not guarantee delivery.

best_practices: Pass the caller context as the first parameter and use context-aware downstream APIs.
Release derived contexts on every path unless cancellation ownership is explicitly transferred.
Use typed metadata keys and give detached work an explicit timeout and lifecycle owner.
anti_patterns: Creating a new Background context inside a request call chain.
Using context values to hide database connections, configuration, or required business arguments.
Launching detached goroutines without lifetime limits or shutdown coordination.

faq.question: Which AI tools does this skill support?
faq.answer: The declared supported tools are Codex and Claude Code.

faq.question: Which Go version do the newer context examples require?
faq.answer: WithoutCancel and AfterFunc require Go 1.21 or later. Other application APIs may require newer versions.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically detect every context bug?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and evaluation scenarios, not a standalone analyzer. Compile changes, run tests, and use appropriate linters.

faq.question: What belongs in context values?
faq.answer: Use request-scoped metadata such as trace IDs or authenticated identity. Keep infrastructure dependencies and business arguments explicit.

faq.question: Can a child timeout extend its parent deadline?
faq.answer: No. The earlier deadline applies, so a child cannot extend the time remaining on its parent.

faq.question: Does WithoutCancel guarantee background audit delivery?
faq.answer: No. It only detaches cancellation and deadlines while preserving values. Add a timeout and shutdown coordination; reliable delivery may require durable infrastructure.
